name: Cash-Secured Put
summary: Sell a put while holding enough cash to buy 100 shares at the strike - income now, with a willingness to own the stock lower.

legs.strike_rule: Delta -0.16 to -0.30 (the -0.16 strike approximates the 1-SD expected move)

max_profit: The credit x 100, realised if the put expires OTM
max_loss: (strike - credit) x 100 if the underlying goes to zero. Large but defined and fully cash-collateralised.

greeks.delta: +0.16 to +0.30 (a short put is positive delta)
greeks.vega: negative; the position profits when IV falls, which is why IVR > 30 is the entry gate

when_to_use: IVR > 30 on a liquid underlying you would genuinely be willing to own at the strike. The classic short-premium workhorse and the most capital-appropriate income strategy for a Level 1-3 account.
entry_rules: Cash available >= strike x 100 x contracts. The automation verifies this before submitting; without it the position is a naked put (Level 4)
Credit >= 1% of the strike per 30 days (e.g. >= $1.00 on a $100 strike), otherwise the risk is underpaid
Underlying must be one you are willing to own: ADV >= 2M shares, price > $20, no pending merger, not a leveraged or inverse ETF
No earnings before expiry unless running the explicit post-earnings variant
Per-position notional (strike x 100) <= 20% of equity (~$10,000 on $50k); total short-put notional <= 100% of equity
management_rules: Buy to close at 50% of the credit received - the standard short-premium benchmark: it raises win rate per unit of time and cuts gamma exposure
Or close at 21 DTE, whichever comes first. Gamma risk past 21 DTE is not compensated by the remaining theta

Roll down and out when the short put delta exceeds -0.50: buy back the put and sell a lower strike 30-45 days out FOR A NET CREDIT. If no credit is available, close the position instead of rolling into a bigger one
Do not roll more than twice on the same position. After the second roll, close and accept the loss
Hard stop at 2.5x the credit received (position mid >= 2.5 x entry credit)
exit_rules: Buy to close at 50% of credit, at 21 DTE, or at the 2.5x credit stop, whichever comes first

MANDATORY NEVER-ASSIGN RULE: close or roll the short put whenever (a) it goes ITM and its extrinsic value falls below $0.10, or (b) its delta exceeds -0.85, or (c) on expiration day if the underlying is within 1.0% of the strike as of 14:30 ET. ABSOLUTE BACKSTOP: no short put may be held past 15:45 ET on expiration day under any circumstances

American-style equity puts can be assigned at ANY time. Put early assignment is driven by interest-rate carry and deep-ITM extrinsic collapse rather than dividends, so the extrinsic < $0.10 check must run on every position refresh, not only near expiry
If assignment happens despite the rules, the recovery procedure is: sell the 100 shares at market at the next open, log the breach, and disable new CSPs on that symbol until reviewed
assignment_risk: MODERATE to HIGH depending on how far ITM. Assignment delivers 100 shares at the strike and consumes the collateral cash. The account CAN absorb it (it is cash-secured) but the mandate is never to be assigned, so the triggers above are hard-coded. Unlike calls, put early assignment is not dividend-driven.
buying_power: Cash collateral of strike x 100 per contract, less the credit received. In a margin account Alpaca will typically hold less, but the system should self-impose full cash securing so the position can never become effectively naked.
liquidity_needs: OI >= 500, spread <= 8% of mid, underlying ADV >= 2M shares. You must be able to buy the put back and to roll it.
common_mistakes: Selling puts on a name you do not actually want to own; rolling a loser three or four times and turning a small loss into a large one; holding to expiry hoping a near-the-money put expires worthless, which is exactly how unwanted assignment happens; selling puts when IVR < 20 and being paid nothing for real risk.
zero_dte_notes: See zero-dte-cash-secured-put for the same-day variant.
also_filed_under: Stock/ETF Shares Combined With Options (covered writes, protective hedges, collars, synthetics, repairs, conversions)
